note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), read offline from the bundled owb-am text, per the founder decision of 2026-11-18 that every Amharic work quotes OWB. Every quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim, replacing the 1962 UBS wording and the OT renderings made in its register: the cited verses in each life, the verses recited inside the prose, and the closing Scripture appendix (chapter 13), which quotes each of them again.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse or range, the shortest span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'. `self_rendered` rows (each with a `why`) are allusions, paraphrases and the closing prayers' own petitions. The English edition, an Ochorus Original, quotes the NIV; the Amharic follows OWB's wording even where it differs from the NIV's.

Judgement calls. Luke 18:1 'always' is OWB «ሁልጊዜ», so the author's prose about 'that word always' (ch1, ch2) now says ሁልጊዜ, not ዘወትር. 1 Thessalonians 5:17 is OWB «መጸለይን አታቋርጡ» (decision pray-without-ceasing); Wesley's gloss on the word follows it («አታቋርጡ»), and Colossians 4:2 (OWB «ሳታቋርጡ ጸልዩ፤ ስትጸልዩም ንቁ፤ አመስግኑም።», missed by the detector, ch11 b9 and ch13 b61) keeps the author's devotion/watchful/thankful gloss. Luke 11:1 quotes OWB's whole request «ጌታ ሆይ፣ ዮሐንስ የራሱን ደቀ መዛሙርት እንዳስተማረ፣ እንዴት መጸለይ እንዳለብን አስተምረን», as the other Amharic prayer books do (decision teach-us-to-pray). Hebrews 4:16 'with confidence' is OWB «በመተማመን», so Luther's parrēsia gloss names that word. Psalm 62:8 drops OWB's trailing ሴላ. Minimal prose followed the new words: Ezekiel 22:30 'gap' (በክፍተቱ), Isaiah 62:6 'watchman' (ዘበኛው), Hebrews 7:25 'always' (ሁልጊዜ), 1 Peter 5:7 'cares' (ግድ ይለዋል), James 5:16 'powerful and effective' echoed as «ጸሎቱም ሠራ፤ ብዙ ነገርም አደረገ», and Philippians 4:7 'minds' (አእምሮውን). Ephesians 3:20 recited without marks in the epilogue (ch12 b0) takes OWB's words too.
